This correction is aimed at fixing the offset of `si_pkey` in the `siginfo` structure, which was affected by the previous change that moved `addr_lsb` into the `_sigfault` union. The modifications in `siginfo.h` and `compat.h` are consistent with each other, ensuring that both user-space and compatibility structures reflect the necessary changes for correct functionality.

Here is the commit message:
signal: Correct the offset of si_pkey in struct siginfo

The change moving addr_lsb into the _sigfault union failed to take
into account that _sigfault._addr_bnd._lower being a pointer forced
the entire union to have pointer alignment.  In practice this only
mattered for the offset of si_pkey which is why this has taken so long
to discover.

To correct this change _dummy_pkey and _dummy_bnd to have pointer type.

Reported-by: kernel test robot <shun.hao@intel.com>
Fixes: b68a68d3dcc1 ("signal: Move addr_lsb into the _sigfault union for clarity")
Signed-off-by: "Eric W. Biederman" <ebiederm@xmission.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect alignment of the `_sigfault` union in the `siginfo` structure due to the change that moved `addr_lsb` into the union without properly accounting for the pointer alignment requirements. This oversight led to the miscalculation of the offset for `si_pkey`, which is critical for the correct functioning of signal handling related to segmentation faults and protection key violations.

Here is the patch:
 				/* used when si_code=SEGV_BNDERR */
 				struct {
-					short _dummy_bnd;
+					void *_dummy_bnd;
 					void __user *_lower;
 					void __user *_upper;
 				/* used when si_code=SEGV_PKUERR */
 				struct {
-					short _dummy_pkey;
+					void *_dummy_pkey;
 					__u32 _pkey;
 				} _addr_pkey;
